responses_compaction._comment: Optional OpenAI-native compaction for the Responses API only. Torana adds context_management when the caller did not provide it. Omit this block to disable; Chat Completions requests are never changed.

local-slm._comment: Local OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio). Point offload here to summarize tool output on a self-hosted small model at zero marginal cost. Ollama serves the OpenAI API at http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions, so set url to the host root. Providers may also set 'api_key_env' naming an env var with their own API key — required for plugin-initiated rerouting (env.route_request), where the caller's credential is never forwarded; leave it unset for local endpoints that need no auth.

gemini._comment: Public Gemini API (or Vertex AI) over the bare Gemini generateContent wire format — for tools you point at a base URL with an API key (Cline, Aider, Continue, Zed, opencode, …), exactly like the openai providers. No MITM needed: send requests to /provider/gemini/v1beta/models/<model>:streamGenerateContent. Set api_key_env if rerouting here; otherwise the caller's key/credential is forwarded.

antigravity._comment: Google Code Assist backend for the Antigravity CLI (agy), reached via the MITM ingress below (agy can't be pointed at a base URL). Same content model as 'gemini' but wrapped in the Code Assist envelope, hence format 'gemini-codeassist'. The caller's own Google OAuth bearer is forwarded upstream — Torana injects no auth. Two channels exist: prod (this) and 'daily' (dev); the mitm.hosts map routes each hostname to the matching provider.

mitm._comment: TLS-terminating CONNECT proxy for harnesses that can't be pointed at a base URL (the Antigravity CLI's stripped Go binary ignores endpoint env vars but honors HTTPS_PROXY and a custom CA via SSL_CERT_FILE). Disabled unless 'enabled' is true. Only chat calls (…:streamGenerateContent / …:generateContent) on the mapped hosts run through the provider pipeline; all other hosts and paths are tunneled/forwarded verbatim so login and telemetry keep working. Point agy at it with HTTPS_PROXY=http://<listen> SSL_CERT_FILE=<ca_dir>/bundle.pem. 'listen' is restricted to a literal loopback address because it decrypts caller traffic. NEVER commit ca_dir (the CA private key lives there) or add the CA to the system trust store.

plugins._comment: order is empty because this file has to start a Torana that has no plugins installed yet — naming a plugin whose bundle is absent is a hard startup failure, by design, so a missing plugin is never silently ignored. IMPORTANT: this file is only read on FIRST start. Torana copies it into a managed store (~/.config/torana/config.json, or $TORANA_DATA_DIR/config.json) and reads that from then on, so editing this file later changes nothing. To enable plugins: install them with 'torana plugin install --official', then approve, enable and order them in the control plane at http://127.0.0.1:8080/_torana/. Only edit this file before the first start. A safe coding-agent baseline is ["schema_translator", "intent"]; to compact tool results append ONE compactor after intent with explicit ordered tool_policies (unmatched tools stay exact). See docs/COMPACTION.md.

tool_policies.rerun: Repeat the search to recover every result.

offload._comment: Cheap-model tool result summarization used by the compactor plugin. 'provider' must exist above and use the openai format (deepseek-v4-flash is only a default, not a hard dependency — any openai-compatible model works, including a local SLM via the 'local-slm' provider). 'api_key_env' names an env var holding a dedicated offload key. IMPORTANT: leave it empty ONLY when the offload provider shares the caller's auth; for cross-provider offload (e.g. a Claude- or OpenAI-key caller summarizing on DeepSeek) or a keyless local model, set a dedicated key here — otherwise the caller's credential is reused and will fail to authenticate against a different provider.

cache._comment: Cross-request plugin state. The memory backend is TTL+LRU bounded; max_entries defaults to 10000 and max_bytes to 64 MiB. Redis deployments should configure server-side eviction. 'password_env' names the password environment variable — never put the password here.
